correctness.rationale: The final claim removes precisely one oriented signed root, retaining its negative, from P_{p,q} for all p,q>=2. The Cayley representation P=conv(Q,-Q) and s=(1+sum_L x_i)/2 turn the deletion into x_1-x_{p+1}<=s and a cap pyramid. The projection candidate z_H=v-g/||g||^2 has barycentric coefficients q(p+2),p(q+2),2(p+q)-pq divided by pq+4(p+q), so it belongs to the facet precisely through the threshold pq<=2(p+q), with a lower-dimensional point at equality. For pq>2(p+q), the A/B-simplex candidate has positive coefficients; the residual scalar products of every surviving root establish the global KKT projection inequality and yield squared distance pq/[2pq-p-q]. Metric distance convexity gives the directed Hausdorff equality. Simplex-difference mixed-volume coefficients, explicit slice Jacobians 2 and s, and beta integrals yield integer normalized volumes T_{p,q} and E_{p,q}; both use the root lattice normalization (n-1)!vol/sqrt(n). Independent exact-Fraction recalculation for p,q=(2,2),(3,3),(4,4),(5,5),(3,7) reproduces the sums and distance, and the inspected checker explicitly handles 256 p,q pairs plus optional 11 hulls. This is an analytic proof for all p,q, not an extrapolation from that finite sample.

value.rationale: The graph family is a standard canonical family of symmetric edge/root polytopes; deleting a single oriented generator is a natural stability perturbation. The theorem determines two independent sharp invariants (Euclidean vertex robustness/contact-face transition and exact normalized lost volume), including a non-obvious pq=2(p+q) boundary. These are not immediate from the undeleted-volume formula and can serve lattice-geometry and robustness analysis.

limitations: A single oriented deletion only, not both signs; projection contact at threshold belongs to a proper subface despite full facet exposure.
Finite verification does not establish universal all-parameter mixed-volume formulas; they follow from analytic integration.
